title: The Detention of the water tower
premise: Ulyana Nystrom, a trans boy hiding in plain sight at Marrow Creek High, is assigned the school's legendary college essay prompt: 'Who are you when no one is watching?' But the prompt is older than the school itself, and every honest answer feeds the thing sealed beneath the water tower — an entity that grants belonging by erasing what makes students different. As classmates who answer become eerily 'perfect,' Ulyana realizes his truth could either free them or feed it. In the end, he answers aloud, unedited and unashamed, breaking the tower's hold — but not before losing someone he loves to its promise of effortless acceptance.
about_author: Tamsin Yarrow grew up in a mill town where the water tower was the tallest thing for miles, and she never stopped wondering what it watched. She writes stories about kids who refuse to be edited.

chapters.title: Head Down
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Three weeks into Marrow Creek High, he has perfected invisibility: correct pronouns avoided by avoiding conversation entirely. A glimpse of the rusted water tower through the gym window unsettles him. Emotional beat: the exhausting safety of being no one.

chapters.title: The Prompt
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. English teacher Ms. Okonkwo unveils the senior essay prompt, unchanged for sixty years: 'Who are you when no one is watching?' The class goes strangely quiet; one student, Priya, whispers that her cousin answered it and 'got better.' Beat: dread disguised as routine homework.

chapters.title: Locker 114
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya, sharp-tongued and friendless since her cousin transferred away 'glowing,' warns Ulyana not to write anything true. She shows him the yearbook: six decades of seniors whose photos blur slightly at the edges. Beat: an alliance of the unwilling.

chapters.title: First Draft
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Alone at night, Ulyana writes one true sentence about who he is, then deletes it. The deleted words appear scratched into his desk the next morning. Beat: the horror of being read.

chapters.title: The Better Kids
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Students who submitted drafts early — star athlete Dev, quiet artist Mabel — seem suddenly beloved, seamless, adored. Their old quirks are gone. Priya notices Dev can't remember his own middle name. Beat: uncanny perfection as threat.

chapters.title: Under the Tower
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Priya cut class to investigate the decommissioned water tower behind the school. Inside, they find walls papered with sixty years of essays, all answered in the same handwriting. Beat: awe curdling into violation.

chapters.title: Ms. Okonkwo's Confession
chapters.summary: Ms. Okonkwo's POV. The teacher reveals she answered the prompt as a student in 1994 and has been its custodian ever since, aging wrong, unable to leave town. She begs Ulyana to submit something bland. Beat: complicity across generations.

chapters.title: Dev, Perfect
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. From inside, Dev experiences his transformation as bliss — finally fitting, finally enough. He gently tells Ulyana to stop fighting it. Beat: temptation made sympathetic.

chapters.title: What the Labels Come Off
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. His deadname surfaces on a roster, and the school machine treats him as someone else entirely — records shifting, teachers confused. The entity is editing him preemptively. Beat: identity under siege from systems, not just magic.

chapters.title: Mabel's Last True Thing
chapters.summary: Mabel's POV, fragmenting. Half-erased, Mabel hides one uncorrupted drawing in Ulyana's locker — a picture of the tower weeping ink. It's both warning and map. Beat: resistance flickering inside surrender.

chapters.title: The Essay Deadline
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Submissions are due Friday. Priya proposes burning the essay archive beneath the tower; Ms. Okonkwo warns it takes a fully true answer to unmake it, and no one has survived giving one. Beat: plan vs. prophecy.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Hollow
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. At Homecoming, the 'better' students move like a chorus. Dev wins king without campaigning. Ulyana dances with Priya and feels, briefly, ordinary happiness — which the tower immediately offers to make permanent. Beat: longing weaponized.

chapters.title: Priya Answers
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Grieving her cousin, Priya submits an angry, truthful draft to bait the entity — and vanishes overnight, leaving only a glowing yearbook photo. Beat: guilt and grief detonating.

chapters.title: Interrogation of the Self
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Haunted by Priya's absence, Ulyana interrogates what 'true' even means for someone who's spent years performing a self. His mother finds his old journal; a raw, tender scene of partial coming-out. Beat: the first honest conversation.

chapters.title: The Handwriting
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Ms. Okonkwo compare archives and discover the identical handwriting belongs to the school's founder, who built the tower to 'perfect' a dying town's children — and became its first meal. Beat: history rhyming into trap.

chapters.title: Fifteen Minutes of Truth
chapters.summary: Dev's POV, cracking. A memory leaks through — his real laugh, his real fear — and Dev begs Ulyana, in a bathroom stall whisper, to finish what he started. Then the smoothness reclaims him mid-sentence. Beat: hope snatched back.

chapters.title: Lockdown
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The school seals itself: doors remember other shapes, hallways loop toward the tower. The entity speaks through the PA system, offering Ulyana a painless self, pre-approved. Beat: claustrophobia and the sweetest offer.

chapters.title: What Priya Left
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Following Mabel's drawing, Ulyana finds Priya half-dissolved in the archive wall, still arguing, still herself at the core. She gives him her unfinished essay — rage and love, undiluted. Beat: inheritance of courage.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Climax begins. At Friday's mandatory assembly, each senior must read their essay aloud. One by one, the perfected students recite flawless nothing. Ulyana walks to the podium with two essays in his hands. Beat: held breath.

chapters.title: Answer Honestly
chapters.summary: Climax. Ulyana reads his own truth — name, body, fear, want — then Priya's, then demands the tower take his words instead of their selves. The archive ignites; the entity, fed on honesty it cannot digest, tears open. Dev and Mabel wake; Priya does not fully return. Beat: triumph with a cost.

chapters.title: Aftertaste
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The tower stands empty and ordinary. Ms. Okonkwo ages a year overnight and resigns, freed. The school mourns Priya in a way that finally feels human. Ulyana submits his real essay to colleges — unedited. Beat: grief braided with release.

chapters.title: Who I Am When Everyone Is Watching
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Ulyana's POV. Graduation on the lawn beneath the dry tower. Ulyana reads his accepted college essay aloud at the microphone, by choice this time. Somewhere, faintly, water moves in pipes that should be empty — but he stands anyway. Beat: chosen visibility, vigilance, hope.
